 Gunman who killed at least 6 in Kraków mass shooting has died in hospital
 By Helen Regan 
 Updated Nov 9, 2026, 2:20 AM ET 
 PUBLISHED Nov 9, 2026, 1:11 AM ET 
 Bullet holes in the glass enclosure of a restaurant terrace in the Main Market Square following the Saturday mass shooting in Krakow, Poland, on November 8, 2026. 
 Jakub Porzycki/Reuters

 A gunman who killed at least six people during a deadly rampage in the Polish city of Kraków on Saturday has died in hospital, Reuters news agency reported on Monday, citing police.
 The country was horrified by the rare mass shooting in the historic main square of the city in the country’s south, which prompted national mourning and heightened security, as authorities said the attack was likely driven by far-right ideology.
 The Polish citizen, in his 20s, was shot and injured by police during the attack before being transported to hospital. There, he underwent multiple surgeries and had been in a critical condition prior to his death.
 The mass shooting — which authorities said they are investigating as a possible terror attack — has generated a wave of fear in a European nation with exceptionally tight gun laws.
 Kraków police said the gunman drove into the city’s main market square, typically popular with tourists and locals, and started firing randomly at people, initially from his car, killing four women and two men, on Saturday afternoon. Sixteen others were injured, including two police officers.

 Video captures gunshots from site of deadly shooting in Kraków Poland
 Gunshots can be heard on social media video from Krakow, Poland, where at least 6 people are dead after a man drove onto the square and opened fire from within his vehicle at what appeared to be random people, Krakow police said in a post on X.
 0:29
 • Source:

 Video captures gunshots from site of deadly shooting in Kraków Poland 
 0:29
 The alleged attacker was wearing military-style clothing and used “military weapons,” Police Deputy Inspector Katarzyna Cisło told Polish news outlet TVN24. Weapons and ammunition were also found in his vehicle.
 The bodies of his sister, mother and father were later found at the suspect’s home in the town of Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, about 120 miles northeast of Kraków. Poland’s prosecutor’s office said Sunday that it is “highly likely” the killings were carried out by the same person, but investigations were ongoing.
 Eleven firearms were recovered from both sites, the prosecutor’s office spokesperson said.
 Gunman’s clothing examined
 Little is known about the gunman, who has not been identified by police, and his motive was not immediately clear. But Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said that the shooter was fascinated with far-right ideologies and held “very radical views.”
 Emblems on his clothing were being examined by experts, an interior ministry spokesperson said on Monday.
 “These patches were associated with various motifs that are currently being analyzed by specialists,” Karolina Galecka told radio TOK FM, Reuters reported.
 Related article
 People embrace one another near the Main Market Square the day after a mass shooting in Krakow, Poland, November 8, 2026. 
 Jakub Porzycki/Reuters 
 Poland stunned as suspect with far-right views kills 6 in Kraków mass shooting 
 5 min read 
 The suspect was a member of a shooting club and appeared to be highly skilled marksman, the club spokesperson Adam Chyb told Reuters on Sunday.
 Poland, like other European Union countries, has strict rules about acquiring guns and very few people are allowed to own military-style weapons or carry guns in public. About 411,000 people have gun permits in the country, which has a population of more than 37 million, according to the Associated Press.
 Off-duty surgeons saved lives
 An off-duty surgeon who rushed to the scene of the shooting to treat victims of the attack, including a police officer, said he had just finished eating lunch with his family when he heard “what sounded like gunshots.”
 Michal Pedziwiatr described being “in the eye of the storm” as he and a friend – also a surgeon – began providing care to the wounded.
 Pedziwiatr told a press conference on Sunday that his friend, Mateusz Wierdak, was a “hero” for saving the life of a police officer who subdued the attacker, after he “applied pressure to the bleeding wound without any protective gear or gloves” and “stuffed gauze pads into the chest cavity,” Reuters reported.
 The two wounded police officers, who Polish Prime ​Minister ‌Donald Tusk praised for also saving “many lives,” underwent surgery and remain in hospital, police said.
 This is a developing story and will be updated. 
 CNN’s Charlotte Reck, Christina Zdanowicz, Billy Stockwell and Sana Noor Haq contributed reporting.
